title: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: Russia invasion of Ukraine
sections.summary: The past week saw Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the largest war in Europe since World War II.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the past week, we have witnessed Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the largest war on the European continent since World War II.

sections.label: Ukraine fighting alone
sections.summary: Ukraine had to fight alone against a more heavily armed neighbour, reminding small countries they cannot assume others will assist them in war.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Yet, when the time for fighting came, despite wide-spread condemnation from the international community, Ukraine had to fight alone against a much more heavily armed neighbour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is an important reminder to all countries, particularly small ones like us, that we cannot assume other countries will come to our assistance when we are at war and we have to do all we can to defend ourselves.

sections.label: US-China rivalry and Taiwan
sections.summary: US-China rivalry is intensifying in trade and technology regulations, with stronger rhetoric and action over Taiwan as a likely conflict catalyst.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The US-China rivalry has continued to intensify and we see that this is increasingly playing out in both countries' regulations in the trade and technology domains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have also seen stronger rhetoric and action over Taiwan and this seems to be an increasingly likely catalyst if a conflict, intended or otherwise, were to break out between the two powers.

sections.label: Foreign info-operations messages
sections.summary: Messages in chat groups seemed targeted at swaying Singapore public opinion and may be part of foreign info-operations, prompting a question to the Minister for Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Although Singapore is far away from the Russia-Ukraine conflict, I have seen messages being circulated in chat groups that seemed to be targeted at swaying public opinion in Singapore and I have my suspicions that such messages may be part of an info-operations exercise by foreign actors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence comment on some of the trends in our security environment that MINDEF is watching?

sections.label: SAF vaccination rate
sections.summary: The SAF has now vaccinated almost 100% of its soldiers, sailors and airmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The SAF has now vaccinated almost 100% of its soldiers, sailors and airmen.

sections.label: NS training during pandemic
sections.summary: Basic Military Training and NS call-ups were suspended early in the pandemic, and MINDEF later spoke about resuming overseas training and large-scale exercises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the early phase of the pandemic, Basic Military Training and National Service (NS) call-ups had to be suspended for a while.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last year, MINDEF spoke about the resumption of some overseas training and large-scale exercises, after implementing stringent testing and safe management measures.

sections.label: Exercise Wallaby 2021 limited scale
sections.summary: Exercise Wallaby concluded in 2021 but was limited in scale due to virus transmission concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Even while SAF successfully concluded Exercise Wallaby in 2021, the scale of the exercise was limited, due to concerns relating to the transmission of the virus.

sections.label: Pandemic disruptions to SAF training
sections.summary: Dr Ng Eng Hen said the pandemic disrupted SAF training, with steady progress resuming In-Camp Training and exercises via safe measures and testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: At the COS debate last year, Minister for Defence Dr Ng Eng Hen talked about disruptions to SAF's training activities as a result of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: He highlighted that there had been steady progress on resuming In-Camp Training and exercises, enabled by strict safe management measures and robust testing.

sections.label: Russian invasion and Singapore defence
sections.summary: The Russian invasion of Ukraine reminds Singapore of the importance of a strong defence force as a deterrent against foreign aggression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The recent Russian invasion of Ukraine is a reminder to us of the importance of Singapore having a strong defence force as an effective deterrent against foreign aggression and ambitions.

sections.label: Shrinking cohorts and new technologies
sections.summary: Shrinking fertility means smaller National Service cohorts, while AI, digital analytics and Internet of Things offer SAF force-multiplier opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As a small country with a shrinking total fertility rate, we can expect subsequent National Service cohorts to similarly decrease in size in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: At the very same time, new technologies arising from the fourth Industrial Revolution, such as artificial intelligence (AI), digital analytics and the Internet of Things, offer new opportunities for SAF to leverage as a force multiplier to overcome manpower limitations.

sections.label: Next-Generation SAF transformation update
sections.summary: The Minister for Defence is asked to update the House on Next-Generation SAF transformation, as full-time National Servicemen numbers are projected to decrease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence update the House on the progress of the transformation efforts towards the Next-Generation SAF?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: The number of full-time National Servicemen is projected to decrease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: MINDEF and SAF will need to do more with less.

sections.label: MINDEF unmanned technologies and AI
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked about plans to intensify unmanned technologies and incorporate AI into defence plans despite a declining population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Can MINDEF update on its plans to develop and intensify the use of unmanned technologies to ensure our defence strategies remain robust despite our declining population?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: How has MINDEF developed its concepts of operations to incorporate such unmanned technologies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: How has MINDEF incorporated AI also into its defence plans?

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat agreement
sections.summary: The recent agreement signed at the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat is cited as a good case in point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The recent agreement signed at the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders’ Retreat is a good case in point.

sections.label: Retreat agreements and defence cooperation
sections.summary: The first post-pandemic Retreat saw three agreements under the Expanded Framework, including a Joint Statement on the 2007 DCA and its Implementation Arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Not only was the Retreat significant because it was the first Retreat since the COVID-19 pandemic, it was also successful in that it saw the signing of three sets of agreements that addressed longstanding bilateral issues under the ambit of the Expanded Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: One of the three agreements signed was a Joint Statement on the 2007 Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA) and its Implementation Arrangement between SAF and the Indonesian National Defence Forces for the Military Training Area in Indonesia.

sections.label: ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting platform
sections.summary: The ADMM is the region's security platform for open dialogue and practical cooperation to foster regional stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) is the region's security platform to engage in open dialogue and practical cooperation to foster regional stability.

sections.label: ADMM-Plus member countries
sections.summary: ADMM-Plus consists of eight other countries, including China, Russia and the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Further, ADMM-Plus consists of eight other countries, including China, Russia and the US.

sections.label: Ministry spending increase resumption
sections.summary: The Ministry will increase spending relative to the past two years due to resumption of projects, training and exercises disrupted by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This year, my Ministry will increase our spending relative to the past two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: That increase is due to the resumption of projects, training and exercises which were disrupted by COVID-19 over the past two years.

sections.label: MINDEF projected expenditure and growth
sections.summary: With resumption to pre-COVID-19 levels, expenditure is projected at $16.3 billion, a 6.5% one-off catch-up increase, with 3% to 4% nominal growth over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: With the planned resumption of both projects and training to pre-COVID-19 levels in the coming financial year, we are projecting an expenditure of $16.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This translates to an increase of 6.5%, which is expected to be one-off and a catch-up for the reduced spending for FYs 2020 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: COVID-19 resulted in sharp dips and spikes but, over the next five years, MINDEF's budget is expected to keep pace with inflation, or 3% to 4% nominal growth each year, which I have assured this House previously.

sections.label: MINDEF/SAF vaccination and booster rates
sections.summary: 99.7% of MINDEF/SAF personnel are vaccinated and 91% have received their booster shot.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Of our MINDEF/SAF personnel, 99.7% are vaccinated and 91% have received their booster shot.

sections.label: Midlife upgrades and unmanned systems
sections.summary: Midlife upgrades will boost frigate capabilities, and the SAF is acquiring UAVs and deploying unmanned surface vessels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Because each time we do a midlife upgrade, we look at the technology that has evolved, our manpower, the design and, including artificial intelligence, if we can.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: So, after the upgrade, the frigates' combat capabilities will increase and be equipped with better combat management and communication systems, weapons systems, along with improved maintenance processes – basically, to use less to achieve more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The RSAF has acquired the Orbiter 4 Close-Range Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (CR-UAV).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And with their smaller size, capable sensors and increased portability, these can be used for a wide range of operations, in peace and combat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This year, our Navy will deploy the first tranche of Maritime Security Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs) to patrol local waters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) will also replace its Mine Countermeasure Vessels with a fully unmanned system from 2027 onwards.

sections.label: Army, Navy and Air Force 2040 plans
sections.summary: The Army, Navy and next-generation air force will gain new platforms to be more manoeuvrable, lethal and effective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Army will also operationalise the first Hunter Armoured Battle Group later this month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: By 2040, the Army, equipped in the next-generation infantry battalions and new armoured tracked carriers and howitzers, will be more manoeuvrable, able to track and strike faster and harder.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Navy, with Multi-Role Combat Vessels, Invincible-class submarines and USVs will be able to see and strike further at sea and in the depths, to better protect our waters and our sea lines of communication.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The next-generation air force, with F-15s, F-35s and the next generation Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, will be more lethal, versatile and effective to better protect our skies.

sections.label: Fourth service for SAF 2040
sections.summary: A fourth service is needed to complement the existing three services for SAF 2040.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: To complete that SAF 2040, we will need a fourth service to complement the existing three services.

sections.label: Cyber attack examples cited
sections.summary: Members cited ransomware on the Colonial Pipeline and hacked payment systems in Iran as real-life examples.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Again, I do not think anyone here would gainsay this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We already have real-life examples that exemplify this truth and Members have quoted it: fuel shortages across the US East Coast last May due to ransomware attacks on the Colonial Pipeline; Iranians could not top up their gas and petrol stations last October because the payment systems were hacked.

sections.label: Defence Cyber Organisation and community
sections.summary: A community was built to enhance network resilience, and the Defence Cyber Organisation was set up in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We built up that community to enhance the resilience of our networks and systems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We set up the Defence Cyber Organisation (DCO) in 2017, to coordinate cyber security across the defence sector, and Members of Parliament have filed questions and I have given updates.

sections.label: New Digital and Intelligence Service
sections.summary: The conclusion is that a new fourth service, the Digital and Intelligence Service, best encapsulates the fourth arm of the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Figuratively, if the digital force is now a battalion force, we actually need a few brigades, perhaps even a Division-size force.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our conclusion is that a new fourth service – the Digital and Intelligence Service, or DIS – best encapsulates this fourth arm of the SAF.

sections.label: Germany Cyber and Information Domain Service
sections.summary: Germany established the Cyber and Information Domain Service, consolidating its Communication and Information Systems Command and Geo-information Centre, with setup expected by last quarter this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Germany, for example, has established the Cyber and Information Domain Service, consolidating its Communication and Information Systems Command and Geo-information Centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, we expect to set it up by the last quarter of this year.

sections.label: Functional assessments in pre-enlistment screening
sections.summary: Functional assessments will now be used as part of pre-enlistment medical screening to optimise manpower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: First, to optimise our precious manpower resource, we will now use functional assessments as part of the pre-enlistment medical screening.

sections.label: NS pay, Make-Up Pay, HOME awards
sections.summary: Base NS pay is $1,600 monthly, over 100,000 NSmen and 25,000 employers benefit from automated Make-Up Pay claims, and NS HOME awards increase by $2,000 cash.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The base NS pay is set at $1,600 per month and prorated for the duration of NS call-ups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Over 100,000 NSmen and 25,000 employers will benefit from the automated Make-Up Pay claims and base NS Pay.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Third, we will increase the NS HOME awards, with higher cash components – an extra $2,000 in cash to each National Serviceman.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia Defence Cooperation Agreement
sections.summary: In January, Indonesian Defence Minister Prabowo Subianto and the speaker signed a Joint Statement to bring into force the 2007 DCA and its Implementing Arrangement for a Military Training Area.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In January, Indonesian Defence Minister Prabowo Subianto and I signed a Joint Statement on our agreement to bring into force the 2007 Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA) and its Implementing Arrangement between SAF and the Indonesian Armed Forces for the Military Training Area in Indonesia.

sections.label: SAF COVID-19 and regional assistance
sections.summary: During Delta and Omicron resurgences, MINDEF and SAF assisted MOH, stood up the Home Recovery Task Group, and coordinated transfer of over 500 tonnes of oxygen to Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: When Singapore experienced a resurgence of cases due to the Delta and Omicron variants, MINDEF and SAF personnel were called upon to assist MOH to provide operations planning capabilities, staff contact tracing, call centres or to man emergency departments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: SAF also stood up the Home Recovery Task Group to better manage the home recovery programme for patients, and NSmen also helped as Home Vaccination Teams and Mobile Vaccination Teams.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Last year, SAF’s Changi Regional Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Coordination Centre coordinated the transfer of medical equipment and supplies to regional countries worst hit by COVID-19, including the shipment of over 500 tonnes of oxygen at Indonesia’s request as part of the "Oxygen Shuttle" programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, let me thank Members of this House for their steadfast commitment and support for a robust national defence through a strong SAF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This year, particularly because of the events in Ukraine, I think Singaporeans need less convincing that it is our collective responsibility to keep Singapore safe and secure for ourselves and successive generations.

sections.label: SAF medical classification system review
sections.summary: MINDEF said the review will focus on operational effectiveness of each individual instead of combat-fit or non-combat-fit classification.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But as long as I am fit, I will not hesitate to don my uniform again to help my fellow Singaporeans to defend our country.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This is my country, my home and soil.” As long as we have Singaporeans who share the deep resolve and conviction that Mr Tee and Mr Cheng shared, then, I say, our future remains secure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Chairman, at the COS debate last year, the Minister for Defence mentioned that the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) would use, update and refresh the medical classification system to better match vocations and deployment of National Servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: According to the factsheet published on 1 March 2020, MINDEF claimed that the review will focus on the operational effectiveness of each individual instead of a binary classification of whether one is combat-fit or non-combat-fit.

sections.label: Functional assessments for servicemen deployability
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How shared about reviewing the use of functional assessments to determine servicemen's deployability in specific vocations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: At the last Committee of Supply (COS), Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How shared about reviewing the use of functional assessments to determine our servicemen's deployability in specific vocations.

sections.label: MINDEF ITE Work-Study Diploma
sections.summary: Two years ago, MINDEF announced and launched the Work-Study Diploma with the Institute of Technical Education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Two years ago, MINDEF announced and launched the Work-Study Diploma with the Institute of Technical Education.

sections.label: Civilian expertise in new roles
sections.summary: In March 2019, MINDEF announced that specialised civilian expertise will be harnessed and deployed into new roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In March 2019, MINDEF announced that specialised civilian expertise will be harnessed and deployed into new roles.

sections.label: NS digital transformation plan update
sections.summary: MINDEF announced an NS digital transformation plan, including consolidating digital services for the NS journey into a single platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Last year, MINDEF announced that it had established an NS digital transformation plan, including plans to consolidate digital services for the NS journey into a single platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Would MINDEF please provide an update on this plan and elaborate on how it would improve or enhance the NS experience of our servicemen?

sections.label: NS Review Committee focus areas
sections.summary: When MINDEF announced the creation of the NS Review Committee in 2020, one focus area was NS Recognition and Engagement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: When MINDEF announced the creation of the NS Review Committee in 2020, one of the focus areas announced was "NS Recognition and Engagement".

sections.label: External Review Panel on SAF Safety
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked for an update on the third External Review Panel on SAF Safety's findings so far.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the COS debate last year, Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How said that a third External Review Panel on SAF Safety had been commissioned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could MINDEF provide an update on the panel's findings so far?

sections.label: SAF Inspector-General's Office audits
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked for an update on the SAF IGO's audit findings and resulting training safety measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The SAF Inspector-General’s Office, or IGO in short, plays an important role in strengthening safety and the safety culture in the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I understand that the IGO conducts independent safety audits and inspections within the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would MINDEF provide an update on the SAF IGO's audit findings and the training safety measures that have been introduced in response to its findings?

sections.label: Data and technology for training safety
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked for an update on efforts to use data and technology to strengthen SAF training safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Could MINDEF provide an update on efforts to leverage data and technology to strengthen training safety in the SAF?

sections.label: Clarity for Total Defence support
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked how it will provide clarity so Total Defence is better embraced and supported by all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will MINDEF further provide clarity so that Total Defence will be better embraced and supported by all the people of Singapore?

sections.label: Engaging young people on defence
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked how it has engaged young people on defence and security matters and what initiatives it has embarked on.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: How has MINDEF engaged our young people on defence and security matters?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: What are some of the initiatives that MINDEF has embarked on to ensure that our next generation remains concerned about Singapore's defence?

sections.label: Outreach efforts and defence accessibility
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked about the progress of these initiatives and how to make defence issues accessible and relatable to all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: What are some of these initiatives and how have these outreach efforts progressed?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: How can we encourage Singaporeans from all walks of life to learn and care about defence issues, and also make these issues more accessible and relatable to the man on the street?

sections.label: MINDEF National Education plans
sections.summary: Asks whether MINDEF would update the House on plans to strengthen National Education and how the SDC would support this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Would MINDEF update the House on how it plans to strengthen National Education and how the SDC would continue to support this objective through its programmes and plans?

sections.label: ACCORD community relations role
sections.summary: States ACCORD, since 1984, has built a bridge to the community to provide feedback on Singapore's defence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Advisory Council on Community Relations in Defence (ACCORD), since its inception in 1984, has been instrumental in building this bridge to the community to provide feedback on Singapore’s defence.

sections.label: ACCORD new 2021 members
sections.summary: States ACCORD welcomed new members in 2021 who will bring fresh perspectives given their rich and diverse backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: ACCORD has welcomed new members in 2021 who will, undoubtedly, bring fresh perspectives to issues on defence and community relations, given their rich and diverse backgrounds.

sections.label: Ukraine conflict defence lesson
sections.summary: States the recent conflict in Ukraine underscored how important it is for Singapore to never lose its ability to defend itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The recent conflict in Ukraine has underscored how important it is for countries like Singapore to never lose our ability to defend and look after ourselves.

sections.label: NS 55 years, ACCORD update
sections.summary: Notes NS would have been implemented 55 years on 17 March and asks MINDEF for an update on ACCORD's efforts to shore up support for NS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Come 17 March, NS would have been implemented in Singapore for 55 years already.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could MINDEF please provide an update on ACCORD's efforts to better shore up support for NS?

sections.label: SAF functional assessments for NSFs
sections.summary: States the SAF has implemented functional assessments for full-time National Servicemen to complement existing medical screening processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The SAF has implemented functional assessments for our full-time National Servicemen, or NSFs, to complement our existing medical screening processes.

sections.label: Functional assessments for Transport Operators
sections.summary: A 2021 trial of functional assessments for Transport Operators improved deployment, leading to their implementation for pre-enlistees with orthopaedic conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Our trial on functional assessments for the Transport Operator vocation in 2021 has improved our deployment process and enabled more NSFs to be safely deployed as Transport Operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Riding on this success, we have implemented functional assessments for pre-enlistees with orthopaedic conditions.

sections.label: Work-Learn scheme enrolment numbers
sections.summary: 130 Servicemen enrol yearly in Work-Learn schemes, with 500 expected yearly at steady state in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Four years on, there are now 130 Servicemen enrolling in Work-Learn schemes every year, serving as cyber specialists, as well as Air Force and Army Technicians.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: At steady state in 2025, we expect 500 Servicemen to enrol in Work-Learn schemes every year.

sections.label: Expertise Conversion Scheme renamed
sections.summary: The Expertise Conversion Scheme, launched in 2014, is expanded across all levels and renamed the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: When we launched the Expertise Conversion Scheme, or ECS, in 2014, the landscape was one where expert roles tended to be at the officer level.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Eight years on, we have expanded beyond that and we have expanded expertise deployment across all levels, including roles that are assumed by Warrant Officers, Specialists and Enlistees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And for this reason, we will also rename the ECS into the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

sections.label: In-Camp Training payment for NSmen
sections.summary: Starting later this year, all NSmen will receive at least $1,600 for every month of required In-Camp Training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Starting later this year, all NSmen will receive at least $1,600 for every month of In-Camp Training that they are required to attend.

sections.label: OneNS platform first phase
sections.summary: The first phase of the OneNS platform will be rolled out later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about how MINDEF would leverage technology to improve NS processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that the first phase of the OneNS platform will be rolled out later this year.

sections.label: NS recognition benefits via LifeSG
sections.summary: By mid-2022, MINDEF and MHA will disburse NS recognition benefits to 100,000 National Servicemen yearly via LifeSG.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: By mid-2022, MINDEF and MHA will disburse NS recognition benefits to 100,000 National Servicemen via LifeSG every year.

sections.label: NS HOME awards enhancement
sections.summary: NS HOME awards will be enhanced with an additional $2,000 in cash per National Serviceman across the three existing milestones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As mentioned by the Minister for Defence, we will enhance the NS HOME awards to better express our appreciation to our National Servicemen and their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We will disburse an additional $2,000 in cash to each National Servicemen cumulatively across the three existing NS HOME milestones, comprising $1,000 in cash at the first milestone and $500 in cash each, at the second and third milestones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Our National Servicemen will now receive at least $6,000 at the end of their full-time National Service and at least $5,500 at the mid-point and at the completion of their ORNS journey.

sections.label: Servicemen insurance coverage
sections.summary: The change will benefit 54,000 SAF and Home Team servicemen yearly, with core insurance coverage purchased since 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The change will benefit 54,000 SAF and Home Team servicemen every year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since 2016, MINDEF and MHA have been purchasing Group Term Life and Group Personal Accident core insurance coverage for all MINDEF and MHA servicemen, for a sum assured of $150,000 each.

sections.label: Safety Information System development
sections.summary: MINDEF is developing an enterprise Safety Information System for commanders to share safety trends and lessons across the SAF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Dr Wan Rizal also asked how MINDEF harnesses technology and digitalisation to further strengthen training safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We are developing an enterprise Safety Information System for commanders to disseminate information on safety trends and lessons across the SAF.

sections.label: Open reporting and safety centre
sections.summary: Open reports rose 20% since June, over 37,000 users viewed SafeGuardian information, and a Heat Resilience centre will be established.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since its roll-out to our active Servicemen in June last year, we have seen a 20% increase in open reports being filed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Besides open reporting, we are also encouraged that over 37,000 users have viewed the SafeGuardian’s in-application safety information thus far.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: MINDEF/SAF will be collaborating with DSO and the National University of Singapore to establish the Heat Resilience and Performance Centre in the middle of this year.

sections.label: Six pillars of defence
sections.summary: The six pillars of defence working in concert have allowed Singapore to respond to threats jeopardising its future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The six pillars of defence – military, economic, social, civil, digital, and psychological – working in concert have allowed us to respond to the threats that jeopardise Singapore's future.

sections.label: Vaccination and booster rates
sections.summary: 91% of the total population is fully vaccinated and 68% have received booster shots.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, 91% of our total population is fully vaccinated and 68% have received their booster shots.

sections.label: Kranji Community Facility for migrant workers
sections.summary: MINDEF and partners set up the Kranji Community Facility in May as a temporary migrant worker dormitory, vaccination care centre and community care facility, serving over 70,000 workers over 20 months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MINDEF, together with other MINDEF-related organisations, and more than 20 partners, set up the Community Facility at Kranji in May that year − a temporary dormitory for migrant workers, which also served as a vaccination care centre and community care facility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: It served over 70,000 migrant workers over 20 months.

sections.label: Making Total Defence more inclusive
sections.summary: Total Defence will be made less prescriptive and more inclusive by encouraging more ground-up and community-led efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For one, we will work to make Total Defence less prescriptive and more inclusive, by encouraging more ground-up and community-led efforts.

sections.label: MINDEF youth engagement campaign
sections.summary: Asked by MP Rachel Ong about youth engagement, MINDEF launched a two-year campaign beginning with the Total Defence Sandbox initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Member of Parliament Rachel Ong asked what MINDEF is doing to engage youths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year, we have launched a two-year campaign, beginning with the Total Defence Sandbox initiative.

sections.label: SDC energy and museum experiences
sections.summary: Over 60% of SDC's energy use comes from renewable energy and SDC is working on becoming net carbon-neutral, while capabilities and technology are being developed for more interactive museum experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, more than 60% of its energy use comes from renewable energy and SDC is working on becoming a net carbon-neutral facility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In the next few years, Singaporeans will have more to look forward to in our museums.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We are developing capabilities and investing in technology to make the visitor experience in our three military museums, SDC and the upcoming NS Gallery at Marina Bay more fun and interactive.

sections.label: Refresh of MINDEF volunteer programme
sections.summary: MINDEF has embarked on a refresh of its volunteer programme, with Singaporeans soon able to contribute as educators, researchers and guides in its museums.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MINDEF has also embarked on a refresh for our volunteer programme and Singaporeans will soon be able to contribute in different capacities, including as educators, researchers and guides in our museums.

sections.label: ACCORD support for NSmen
sections.summary: ACCORD will step up efforts to recognise, support and appreciate NSmen, expanding on members' ideas and enhancing the We Support NS Campaign with business discounts and privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: ACCORD, for one, will step up efforts to recognise, support and appreciate NSmen across the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Last year, ACCORD members raised several ideas on how Singaporeans can show their support for NS and we will expand on some of them this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will enhance the "We Support NS Campaign" where businesses, for one, can offer discounts and privileges to NSmen.

sections.label: Training and upskilling reservists
sections.summary: A speaker asks what steps will be taken to train reservists and upskill them amid 4G Army changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One is in relation to the 4G Army and the development, I think the changes are quite interesting to hear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I just want to check what steps will be taken to train reservists and upskill them.

sections.label: Keeping servicemen current during modernisation
sections.summary: The reply says militaries face keeping servicemen current, and focus is on NSFs operating systems at a push of a button.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Most militaries will face that problem as they modernise – how do they keep their Servicemen current.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I think the honest reply is that we focus on the core, which is your NSFs, to make sure that they can, at the push of a button, operate the systems.

sections.label: ATEC and NSmen training levels
sections.summary: ATEC is done before MINDEF Reserve or the 10-year cycle, and NSmen training is expected at pre-COVID-19 levels later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Most NSmen will know that you have ATEC, your tactical evaluation, which is done before they go into MINDEF Reserve (MR) or before they finish the 10-year cycle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The question of training – I think we have talked about it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We will expect to be at pre-COVID-19 levels for NSmen later this year.
